title: Hollow Peak claims conversation intake - scratchpad
content:
Meeting: Hollow Peak initial technical intake (60m)
Date: 2026-03-09
Attendees: Hollow Peak - Lena Brooks (CTO), Omar Diaz (Lead eng), Priya Shah (Claims ops) ; Redwood - Aisha Patel (CS), Marco Nguyen (Solutions), Sofia Romero (SRE)

TL;DR:
- Hollow Peak runs a conversational claims intake flow (phone -> STT -> LLM) to triage, extract entities, recommend claim paths. They want a private deployment behind VPC with strict KMS/HSM requirements and 99.9% availability SLA.
- Primary goals: reduce manual triage by 40%, speed first-touch decisioning to <2m, p95 response latency <= 150ms for model inference step.
- Big constraints: PHI/PII in transcripts, scanned attachments (images/PDFs) associated with calls, intermittent batch replays for audits, and bursty traffic after storms (10x baseline).

Notes / raw capture:
- Current system: Twilio recording -> 3rd-party STT (proprietary, sometimes messy) -> in-house rules engine -> manual claim handler. They want to replace rules+manual step with LLM-assisted triage and structured extraction.
- Call volume baseline: 120 calls/hr (average 15s of text per call). Peak storm: ~1200 calls/hr for ~6 hours.
- Latency budget: total end-to-end from STT result to triage decision = 2 minutes; inference target p95 <= 150ms is for Redwood inference only (they accept some routing/queueing).
- Throughput target for POC: sustain 500 concurrent inference streams (not full token rate) — rough; need to validate with load profile (we asked for transcripts sample).
- Data residency: US-only; contractual ban on copying raw transcripts outside customer VPC/enclave.
- Security: require KMS for model keys & customer keys; HSM option for signing and audit logs. Audit trail preservation for 7 years (regulatory).

Functional requirements (customer-stated):
1) Entity extraction from conversational transcripts: claimant name, policy id, incident date, location, claimed amount, injury classification. Output as JSON schema (they showed an example).
2) Triage classification: severity high/medium/low, route to desk A/B/C, or escalate to human.
3) Confidence scoring for each extraction and classification (they need to gate auto-acceptance).
4) Attachment handling: for PDFs/images uploaded post-call, want image->OCR -> cross-check with extracted entities, mark conflicts.
5) Audit replay: ability to re-run past transcripts through model variants (for drift detection / litigation).

Non-functional / ops requirements:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) preferred, option for Dedicated if necessary. Must support static egress IPs for 3rd-party STT callbacks.
- Sizing: need autoscaling with burst capacity; predictable commit could be reserved GPUs.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-call latency traces, model-level drift alarms, and label/ground-truth ingestion for evals.
- Access: RBAC for ops vs. claims supervisors; audit logs exported to their SIEM (Splunk).

Gotchas / red flags we flagged during call:
- STT quality: filler words, disfluencies, speaker overlaps — causes entity extraction errors. Need to (a) request sample transcripts with timestamps, (b) prefer near-real-time streaming STT that keeps punctuation, or consider running our own STT in private deploy.
- Long contexts: some calls have long back-and-forth (1000+ tokens). KV cache persistence and memory management required. Should ask: expected average tokens per inference call and worst-case tokens.
- Privacy: they explicitly forbid storing raw transcripts outside their controlled storage. Must ensure our caching and any debug logs are stored in customer-managed buckets; default hosted telemetry not allowed.
- Attachment correlation: scanned PDFs often don't OCR well; will need manual review fallback. Integration point for attachments unclear — where do they upload? (we need API shape).
- Legal: litigation hold / discovery requests — must support search across replays and redaction.

Preliminary technical recommendations (brainstorm):
- Use Redwood Private in their VPC with customer-managed S3 + KMS. Provide an ingress Lambda (or webhook worker) that pulls Twilio recording metadata, STT text -> push to Redwood endpoint inside VPC.
- Model choice: start with a compact instruction-tuned model (e.g., 13B quantized perf variant) for extraction/classification for cost reasons; retain a higher-quality 33B variant as fallback for low-confidence cases. Leverage automatic fallback routing by confidence thresholds.
- Cache strategy: persistent KV cache for multi-turn calls (per-call session id), plus prefix caching for common phrases (policy numbers, canned responses). TTL for cached sessions 24h by default, configurable.
- Batch vs streaming: do streaming generation for immediate triage suggestions; for final structured extraction, run short non-streamed completion (faster to get entire JSON).
- Eval plan: build 200 curated transcripts with ground-truth annotations (they have small annotated set of ~50). Run Redwood Optimize to tune quantization + batching to hit p95 latency.

Action items (owners / tentative dates):
- Aisha: Request 100 anonymized sample transcripts + 50 annotated examples from Hollow Peak (ask for redaction/PHI-safe samples) — due 2026-03-16. (ticket: JIRA-CLM-4821)
- Marco: Draft architecture diagram for Private deployment (VPC ingress, KMS flow, SIEM export) and share Confluence page — due 2026-03-15. (confluence: hp-claims-intake)
- Sofia: Estimate GPU sizing for initial POC (500 concurrent streams, p95 150ms) with cost / reserved vs burst options — due 2026-03-18. (internal spreadsheet link pending)
- Hollow Peak (Omar): Confirm attachment upload flow (S3? internal portal?) and provide example PDFs — due 2026-03-17.
- All: Set up 30-min follow-up sync to review sample transcripts and initial sizing — proposed 2026-03-19.

Open questions to resolve with customer:
- Do we need to retain raw audio recordings in their environment indefinitely? (affects storage / egress)
- What's acceptable auto-accept threshold for classification (confidence %)?
- Can they allow ephemeral telemetry with hashed IDs for debugging? If not, we'll need a different tracing approach.
- Will they provide speaker diarization info from STT or should we do speaker-segmentation?

Quick PoC sketch (for internal use):
1) Ingest: webhook -> S3 (customer) -> event triggers Redwood Private HTTP call with session id and transcript text.
2) Inference: primary route -> 13B quantized model for extraction; if confidence < 0.6 -> split to 33B model; output JSON stored back to customer S3 and posted to their claim queue.
3) Audit: log inference inputs+outputs -> store only hashed transcript pointers in Redwood logs; full transcripts remain in customer S3.
4) Monitoring: per-model latency p50/p95, per-field extraction accuracy (post-labeling), cost per 1k calls.

Risks and mitigation:
- Model drift if claims wording changes seasonally -> schedule monthly re-eval runs and auto-alerts for degradation.
- OCR fail on attachments -> build human-in-loop review UI; mark as "needs OCR review" automatically.
- Burst capacity -> contract for reserved baseline + autoscale buffer + fallback routing to smaller models when overloaded.

Notes to self / rough prompts to test for extraction: (very rough)
- "Extract claimant_name, policy_id, incident_date, location, claimed_amount, injury_classification from the transcript. Return JSON with keys and confidence scores."
- Provide several adversarial examples: overlapping speech, policy numbers spoken in pieces, shorthand references ("policy 4-2-1 kinda"), background noise.

Follow-up docs to create (internal):
- PoC runbook (deploy steps, sample data, smoke tests) — assign Marco.
- Data handling compliance checklist for legal (what logs we can store, redaction steps) — assign Aisha + Legal review.
- Prompt suite + eval harness (200 transcripts) for Redwood Optimize — assign Product/Applied ML.

Misc scribbles:
- They asked about offline replay speed: can we bulk-run 10k transcripts overnight? Need batching throughput numbers.
- Should propose SLA tiers: POC non-SLA, Production with 99.9% and 4hr incident response.

End of notes.

-- Aisha (ran out of time mid-call, will follow up on sample format specifics).
